title: C3-UniMM: Causal Cycle-Consistent Unified Multimodal Modeling via Super Alignment and Shared Decoding Space
abstract: arXiv:2608.28603v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Unified Multimodal Models aim to achieve any-to-any understanding and generation across arbitrary modalities. However, existing methods primarily rely on modeling implicit statistical correlations and lack cross-modal structural consistency constraints. This deficiency leads to profound issues, including semantic drift, poor compositional generalization, and instability under interventions. In this paper, we propose C3-UniMM, a unified multimodal modeling framework based on Causal Cycle Consistency and Super Alignment. Specifically, we introduce a Structured Latent Causal Graph (SLCG) as a shared cross-modal semantic space and design unified multimodal encoding blocks, enabling understanding and generation to be synergistically optimized within the identical causal semantic structure. Furthermore, we propose a Unified Decoding Space to enforce structural preservation and semantic invertibility during the cross-modal generation process. T

translated_title: C3-UniMM：基于超级对齐与共享解码空间的因果循环一致性统一多模态建模
translated_abstract: 统一多模态模型旨在实现跨任意模态的任意到任意（any-to-any）的理解与生成。然而，现有方法主要依赖于建模隐式统计相关性，缺乏跨模态结构一致性约束。这一缺陷导致了诸多深层次问题，包括语义漂移、组合泛化能力差以及干预下的不稳定性。在本文中，我们提出了C3-UniMM，一个基于因果循环一致性（Causal Cycle Consistency）与超级对齐（Super Alignment）的统一多模态建模框架。具体而言，我们引入了结构化潜在因果图（SLCG）作为共享的跨模态语义空间，并设计了统一的多模态编码块，使理解与生成能够在相同的因果语义结构内协同优化。此外，我们提出了统一解码空间（Unified Decoding Space），以在跨模态生成过程中强制实现结构保持与语义可逆性。
tldr: 提出基于因果循环一致性与超级对齐的统一多模态框架C3-UniMM，通过结构化潜在因果图构建共享跨模态语义空间，并利用统一解码空间保障结构保持与语义可逆性，从而在统一因果语义结构下协同优化跨模态理解与生成，解决语义漂移和组合泛化差的问题。
en_tdlr: Proposes C3-UniMM, a unified multimodal framework based on causal cycle consistency and super alignment, which introduces a Structured Latent Causal Graph as a shared cross-modal semantic space and a Unified Decoding Space to enforce structural preservation and semantic invertibility, synergistically optimizing cross-modal understanding and generation while addressing semantic drift and poor compositional generalization.
